mechanism_narrative: A persistently high federal funds rate compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces corporate profitability and investor risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% in the prior month signal deteriorating consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve adopts accommodative monetary policy that boosts equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls signals strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 110.0, it indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 110.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% signal a broad-based economic slowdown that erodes corporate revenue growth expectations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decline > 0.5% and HOUST decline > 0.5% in last reporting period
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 200.0 (indicating elevated inflation), the Federal Reserve maintains restrictive monetary policy, compressing equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 200.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.
